This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

Down on 1 and 3, down-up on 2 and 4.

It belongs in *Folk carol*, *Boom-chick*, *Acoustic strum* and *Country train beat*. Here it is in the folk carol style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Strum: downstrokes on the beat

Start with something simpler. One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-strum-quarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Down on 1 and 3, down-up on 2 and 4. Keep the arm moving in eighths: down on every beat, up between. On 1 and 3 the up misses the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}},{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G C|D G|C D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

## How it relates to the other patterns
